questions.question:
The probability that a student knows the correct answer to a multiple choice question is [latex]\frac{2}{3}[/latex]

questions.explanation: Let A be the event when student knows the answer and B be the event when student guesses the answer. Therefore [latex]P(A)=P(A\cap B)=\frac{2}{3} [/latex] [latex]P(B)=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{9}{12}[/latex] where [latex]\frac{2}{3}[/latex] is the probability of correct answer and [latex]\frac{1}{3}[/latex] is the probability that student does not know the answer. So guesses the answer and probability of correct guess is [latex]\frac{1}{4}[/latex]. Therefore total probability of correct answer [latex]=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{9}{12}[/latex] Conditional probability that student knows the correct answer [latex]P(A/B)=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}=\frac{\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{9}{12}}=\frac{8}{9}[/latex]

questions.question:
The solution to the differential equation [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d^{2}u} }{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}-k\frac{\mathrm{du} }{\mathrm{d} x}=0[/latex]
 where k is a constant, subjected to the boundary conditions  u(0) = 0  and  u(L) = U,  is
questions.explanation: We have [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d^{2}u} }{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}-k\frac{\mathrm{du} }{\mathrm{d} x}=0[/latex] [latex](D^2-kD)u=0 [/latex] The auxiliary equation is [latex]\begin{aligned} m^2-km&=0\\ m(m-k)&=0\\ m&=0,k \end{aligned}  [/latex] Thus the complete solution is [latex]\begin{aligned} u&=C_1e^{0x}+C_2e^{kx}\\ u&=C_1+C_2e^{kx} \end{aligned}  [/latex] From given condition [latex] u(0)=0:\;\; C_1+C_2=0 \;\;\;...(i) [/latex] [latex]u(L)=U:\;\; U=C_1+C_2e^{kL}\;\;\;...(ii) [/latex] Subtracting equation (i) from (ii), we get [latex]U=C_2(e^{kL}-1) [/latex] [latex]C_2=\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1} [/latex] From equation (i), we have [latex] C_1=-C_2=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1} [/latex] Substitute these values in the expression for u, we get [latex] u=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1}+\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1}e^{kx}=U\left ( \frac{1-e^{kx}}{1-e^{kL}} \right )[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
We have [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d^{2}u} }{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}-k\frac{\mathrm{du} }{\mathrm{d} x}=0[/latex]
[latex](D^2-kD)u=0 [/latex]
The auxiliary equation is
[latex]\begin{aligned} m^2-km&=0\\ m(m-k)&=0\\ m&=0,k \end{aligned} [/latex]
Thus the complete solution is
[latex]\begin{aligned} u&=C_1e^{0x}+C_2e^{kx}\\ u&=C_1+C_2e^{kx} \end{aligned} [/latex]
From given condition
[latex] u(0)=0:\;\; C_1+C_2=0 \;\;\;...(i) [/latex]
[latex]u(L)=U:\;\; U=C_1+C_2e^{kL}\;\;\;...(ii) [/latex]
Subtracting equation (i) from (ii), we get
[latex]U=C_2(e^{kL}-1) [/latex]
[latex]C_2=\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1} [/latex]
From equation (i), we have
[latex] C_1=-C_2=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1} [/latex]
Substitute these values in the expression for u, we get
[latex] u=\frac{-U}{e^{kL}-1}+\frac{U}{e^{kL}-1}e^{kx}=U\left ( \frac{1-e^{kx}}{1-e^{kL}} \right )[/latex]

questions.question: Water is coming out from a tap and falls vertically downwards. At the tap opening, the stream diameter is 20 mm with uniform velocity of 2 m/s. questions.explanation: Given data: At section 1-1 Diameter: [latex]\quad d_{1}=20 \mathrm{mm}=0.02 \mathrm{m} [/latex] Velocity: [latex] \quad V_{1}=2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} [/latex] Acceleration due to gravity, [latex] g=9.81 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}[/latex] Applying Bernoulli's equation between sections 1 and 2 , we get [latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{p_{1}}{p g}+\frac{V_{1}^{2}}{2 g}+z_{1} &=\frac{p_{2}}{\rho g}+\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{2 g}+z_{2} \\ 0+\frac{V_{1}^{2}}{\rho g}+0.5 &=0+\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{\rho g}+0 \\ \frac{V_{1}^{2}}{2 g}+0.5 &=\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{2 g}\\ \text{ or }\qquad V_{2}^{2}&=V_{1}^{2}+0.5 \times 2 g\\ \text{or }\qquad V_{2} &=\sqrt{V_{1}^{2}+0.5 \times 2 \times g} \\ &=\sqrt{(2)^{2}+0.5 \times 2 \times 9.81} \\ &=\sqrt{13.81}=3.716 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex] Applying continuity equation between sections and 2, we get [latex] \begin{aligned} A_{1} V_{1} &=A_{2} V_{2} \\ \frac{\pi}{4} d_{1}^{2} V_{1} &=\frac{\pi}{4} d_{2}^{2} V_{2}\\ \text{or }\quad d_{1}^{2} V_{1}&=d_{2}^{2} V_{2} \\ (0.02)^{2} \times 2&=d_{2}^{2} \times 3.716\\ \text{or }\quad d_{2}^{2}&=2.1528 \times 10^{-4}\\ \text{or }\quad d_{2} &=0.01467 \mathrm{m} \\ &=14.67 \mathrm{mm} \approx 15 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Applying continuity equation between sections and 2, we get
[latex] \begin{aligned} A_{1} V_{1} &=A_{2} V_{2} \\ \frac{\pi}{4} d_{1}^{2} V_{1} &=\frac{\pi}{4} d_{2}^{2} V_{2}\\ \text{or }\quad d_{1}^{2} V_{1}&=d_{2}^{2} V_{2} \\ (0.02)^{2} \times 2&=d_{2}^{2} \times 3.716\\ \text{or }\quad d_{2}^{2}&=2.1528 \times 10^{-4}\\ \text{or }\quad d_{2} &=0.01467 \mathrm{m} \\ &=14.67 \mathrm{mm} \approx 15 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: In a simple Brayton cycle, the pressure ratio is 8 and temperatures at the entrance of compressor and turbine are 300 K and 1400 K, respectively. Both compressor and gas turbine have isentropic efficiencies equal to 0.8. For the gas, assume a constant value of [latex]c_{p}[/latex] (specific heat at constant pressure) equal to 1 [latex]kJ/kgK[/latex] and ratio of specific heats as 1.4. Neglect changes in kinetic and potential energies. The power required by the compressor in kW/kg of gas flow rate is
questions.explanation: Given data: Pressure ratio, [latex] \begin{aligned} r_{p}&=8\\ T_{1} &=300 \mathrm{K} ; T_{3}=1400 \mathrm{K} \\ \eta_{c} &=\eta_{T}=0.8 \\ c_{p} &=1 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ \gamma &=1.4 \end{aligned}[/latex] For adiabatic isentropic process 1-2s, [latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{T_{2 s}}{T_{1}}&=\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}} \\ \frac{T_{2 s}}{300}&=\left(r_{p}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}=(8)^{\frac{1.4-1}{1.4}}=(8)^{0.2857} \\ \frac{T_{2 s}}{300}&=1.811\\ \text{or }\qquad T_{2 s} &=300 \times 1.811=543.3 \mathrm{K} \\ n_{c} &=\frac{\text { Isentropic rise in temperature }}{\text { Actual rise in temperature }} \\ &=\frac{T_{2 s}-T_{1}}{T_{2}-T_{1}} \\ \therefore \quad 0.8 &=\frac{543.3-300}{T_{2}-300}\\ \text{or }\qquad T_{2}-300&=\frac{243.3}{0.8}=304.12\\ \text{or }\qquad T_{2}&=604.12 \mathrm{K}\\ \end{aligned}[/latex] Power required by compressure, [latex] \begin{aligned} w_{C} &=c_{p}\left(T_{2}-T_{1}\right) \\ &=1(604.12-300) \\ &=304.12 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
Given data:
Pressure ratio,
[latex] \begin{aligned} r_{p}&=8\\ T_{1} &=300 \mathrm{K} ; T_{3}=1400 \mathrm{K} \\ \eta_{c} &=\eta_{T}=0.8 \\ c_{p} &=1 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ \gamma &=1.4 \end{aligned}[/latex]


For adiabatic isentropic process 1-2s,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{T_{2 s}}{T_{1}}&=\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}} \\ \frac{T_{2 s}}{300}&=\left(r_{p}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}=(8)^{\frac{1.4-1}{1.4}}=(8)^{0.2857} \\ \frac{T_{2 s}}{300}&=1.811\\ \text{or }\qquad T_{2 s} &=300 \times 1.811=543.3 \mathrm{K} \\ n_{c} &=\frac{\text { Isentropic rise in temperature }}{\text { Actual rise in temperature }} \\ &=\frac{T_{2 s}-T_{1}}{T_{2}-T_{1}} \\ \therefore \quad 0.8 &=\frac{543.3-300}{T_{2}-300}\\ \text{or }\qquad T_{2}-300&=\frac{243.3}{0.8}=304.12\\ \text{or }\qquad T_{2}&=604.12 \mathrm{K}\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Power required by compressure,
[latex] \begin{aligned} w_{C} &=c_{p}\left(T_{2}-T_{1}\right) \\ &=1(604.12-300) \\ &=304.12 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: In a simple Brayton cycle, the pressure ratio is 8 and temperatures at the entrance of compressor and turbine are 300 K and 1400 K, respectively. Both compressor and gas turbine have isentropic efficiencies equal to 0.8. For the gas, assume a constant value of [latex]c_{p}[/latex] (specific heat at constant pressure) equal to 1 [latex]kJ/kgK[/latex] and ratio of specific heats as 1.4. Neglect changes in kinetic and potential energies. The thermal efficiency of the cycle in percentage (%) is
questions.explanation: For adiabatic process 3-4 s [latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{T_{3}}{T_{4 s}} &=\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}=(8)^{\frac{1.4-1}{1.4}} \\ &=(8)^{0.2857}=1.811 \\ \text{or}\quad T_{4 s} &=\frac{T_{3}}{1.811}=\frac{1400}{1.811} \\ &=773.05 \mathrm{K} \\ \eta_{T} &=\frac{\text { Actual fall in temperature }}{\text { Isentropic fall in temperature }}\\ \eta_{T} &=\frac{T_{3}-T_{4}}{T_{3}-T_{4 s}} \\ 0.8 &=\frac{1400-T_{4}}{1400-773.05} \\ 0.8 &=\frac{1400-T_{4}}{626.95}\\ \text{or }\quad 1400-T_{4}&=0.8 \times 626.95 \\ 1400-T_{4} &=501.56 \\ T_{4} &=898.44 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex] Power developed by the turbine, [latex] \begin{aligned} w_{T} &=c_{p}\left(T_{3}-T_{4}\right) \\ &=1(1400-898.44) \\ &=501.56 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex] Net power output, [latex] \begin{aligned} w_{\text {net }} &=w_{T}-w_{C}=501.56-304.12 \\ &=197.44 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex] Heat supplied, [latex] \begin{aligned} q_{2-3} &=c_{p}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right) \\ &=1(1400-604.12) \\ &=795.88 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex] Thermal efficiency of the cycle, [latex] \begin{aligned} \eta_{\mathrm{th}} &=\frac{\text { Net power output : } w_{\text {net }}}{\text { Heat supplied : } q_{2-3}} \\ &=\frac{197.44}{795.88}=0.2480 \\ &=24.80 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
For adiabatic process 3-4 s
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{T_{3}}{T_{4 s}} &=\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}=(8)^{\frac{1.4-1}{1.4}} \\ &=(8)^{0.2857}=1.811 \\ \text{or}\quad T_{4 s} &=\frac{T_{3}}{1.811}=\frac{1400}{1.811} \\ &=773.05 \mathrm{K} \\ \eta_{T} &=\frac{\text { Actual fall in temperature }}{\text { Isentropic fall in temperature }}\\ \eta_{T} &=\frac{T_{3}-T_{4}}{T_{3}-T_{4 s}} \\ 0.8 &=\frac{1400-T_{4}}{1400-773.05} \\ 0.8 &=\frac{1400-T_{4}}{626.95}\\ \text{or }\quad 1400-T_{4}&=0.8 \times 626.95 \\ 1400-T_{4} &=501.56 \\ T_{4} &=898.44 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Power developed by the turbine,
[latex] \begin{aligned} w_{T} &=c_{p}\left(T_{3}-T_{4}\right) \\ &=1(1400-898.44) \\ &=501.56 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Net power output,
[latex] \begin{aligned} w_{\text {net }} &=w_{T}-w_{C}=501.56-304.12 \\ &=197.44 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Heat supplied,
[latex] \begin{aligned} q_{2-3} &=c_{p}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right) \\ &=1(1400-604.12) \\ &=795.88 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Thermal efficiency of the cycle,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \eta_{\mathrm{th}} &=\frac{\text { Net power output : } w_{\text {net }}}{\text { Heat supplied : } q_{2-3}} \\ &=\frac{197.44}{795.88}=0.2480 \\ &=24.80 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]
